Subject: Trial ops landing plan, infra decision gates & owners

Hi Avery — thanks again for the conversation this morning. Quick written recap and a concrete proposal so we can lock schedules and owners.

Summary of recommended 3-week POC (goal: validate integration, perf/cost, and acceptance criteria):
- Week 0 (prep, 3–7 days): access, account provisioning, security questionnaire, sample data ingest (anonymized).
- Week 1 (baseline & functional): run basic inference flows, validate model outputs on 50 representative prompts, smoke test latency under light concurrency.
- Week 2 (stress & workflows): sustained throughput tests, longer conversations, KV cache validation, cost profiling.
- Week 3 (acceptance & handoff): run acceptance prompts, document regressions, prepare go/no-go readout for your board.

Success criteria (proposed):
- Median token latency <= 300ms for typical conversation length (25–75 tokens) on the selected model variant.
- 95th percentile latency under target concurrency <= 1s.
- End-to-end functional accuracy: no critical functional regressions vs. your baseline on the 50-test prompt set.
- Cost per 1k tokens within the agreed threshold (we'll estimate after we know hosting choice).

Environment options (high level):
1) Hosted API (fastest onboarding) — Redwood-managed, minimal infra setup, suitable if data residency/PHI is not required.
2) Dedicated sandbox (reserved capacity) — predictable throughput, isolation on our infra; quick to provision (1–2 business days) but higher monthly commitment.
3) VPC/Private deployment — customer-managed networking, KMS integration, best for PHI/regulatory requirements; longer lead time (2–3 weeks) and requires infra collaborator on your side.

High-level recommendation: Start the POC on Hosted API to validate baseline functionality and to accelerate the first two weeks; if PHI or audit requirements block that, prioritize VPC and we can run a parallel schedule to hit your calendar.

Attached: trial-ops-outline.pdf — 1-page timeline and owner matrix.

Next asks / actions:
- Avery: confirm whether PHI/data residency is a blocker for Hosted API and share compliance contact.
- ClearPoint: confirm target board readout date (you mentioned early Oct).
- From Redwood: we’ll draft a short SOW and kickoff agenda once you confirm the hosting preference.

Proposed kickoff windows: Tue 2028-09-19 or Thu 2028-09-21, 09:00–11:00 PT. Which works for you?

Thanks — I’ll coordinate owners once you confirm.

—
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
Schedule a time: https://cal.me/sean-redwood

Hi team — quick technical notes on VPC and what ClearPoint should expect. I’m happy to join the kickoff to run the infra checklist.

VPC private deployment (summary):
- Typical lead time: 10–18 business days once we have access and a completed prerequisites sheet. Shorter if we have a named infra contact and SAML/KMS details ready.
- Required items from ClearPoint:
  - VPC peering info or dedicated private subnet details
  - External IP allowlist (if you plan to curl endpoints from your network)
  - KMS/HSM key ARNs and access policy for envelope encryption (optional but recommended for PHI)
  - SSH jump host details for our bootstrap agent (temporary)
  - Contact: infra lead name + email (we need an L1/L2 contact for troubleshooting)
- Testing plans I recommend to validate service:
  - Functional smoke: 50 prompt set (shared) to validate output parity.
  - Load dim: run sustained 10RPS for 30 mins to validate latency SLOs with KV cache warmed.
  - Failure modes: simulated node remove + fallback to model variant to test graceful degradation.

Work effort for Redwood: 2 people 0.5–1.5 days of engineering time to bootstrap, then 1 engineer on-call for the run tests. We’ll also prepare a short runbook for your SREs.

Attached: vpc-prereq-checklist.xlsx — contains the exact fields we need.

If ClearPoint needs a faster path and can accept data de-identification controls and a BAA amendment, Dedicated sandbox is the middle ground and can be provisioned in 1–2 business days. Dedicated removes the need for VPC networking but still gives isolation.

I can estimate cost differential after Sean shares expected token volumes (or expected concurrency).

Karthik
Lead Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
